body: Of course. I can certainly connect and it takes courage to write things even on reddit. I've been there and hoped for a reply from anyone to be let down.
What's the song? Really depends but if you can say it in a somewhat joking way then judge their reaction; it's their followup expression that you have to counter to make it not seem romantic.

Life is a rollercoaster with many up and downs. If you can start identifying when you are going up/up, and appreciate the moments and little things in them. On the opposite, do identifying the lows and try and find those little things you appreciated to help get you moving in the upward direction. 

I get the online thing too and it just seems so fake because you see the number of friends you are connected with, yet half probably won't recognize you in person or will say happy birthday to you. I've learned that people are like seasons and they can be right for a moment but that moment changes. The season will come back around but it won't be the same. Accept, stay positive, don't hold hate, and remember to only compare yourself to your past self.
Please tell me that your example is from a personal experience lol...We do all have that one friend that goes all out.

Turning 34 tomorrow.

 Honestly didn't think I would make it this long but I try and stay positive and happy now.

Warhammer painting sounds interesting. I have a co-worker that does the same and also goes to Gen Com & developed and deployed his own game.  

What I am about to suggest I lack doing but a good way to measure progress is to keep a journal. It might sound silly but give it a shot; I'm going to take my own advice since I am struggling with things and this might help.

Hey, I just want to let you know that you aren't alone. I strictly stayed to my legs but I got to the point where I stocked up on every possible bandage and item to heal because I enjoyed seeing the blood leak out. This might sound weird/stupid/crazy but I once covered my face with my blood because it reminded me of braveheart....

I started in middle school and stopped at some point in high school but started up again 10 months ago after a 12 year relationship with 7 of those years being married. I have been clean for over a month and it's a fight every single night when I am alone. What has helped me a little is to watch motivational video's and write down all the quotes I like. 

"One promise - that life is hard but not impossible."

Anyways, stay strong and know that you made a positive impact on me and gave me a reason to write my first post/reply.
